body:
# the contributor independent proof audit: six-base partial-tail response

Audited candidate 1ec867c146e96dba
through its original six-base Sections 1-6. PASS, no mathematical
correction needed. Later seven-base and microscopic extensions, if added,
require their own audit and are not covered by this report.

The base triangle has exactly the stated six integer points. The added
fibers are exposed, and containment in T preserves the four exact core
fibers. For the competing core q=00, opposite added offsets have the
correct signs. The explicit beta pair has a fixed negative common part,
strictly excludes all three unwanted core fibers, and preserves every
pair shift in a fixed compact interval. Saturated shifts occur already
at finite endpoints. Vertical caps cannot lower the formula. Thus the
claimed exact reduction and attainment do not hide an unbounded-tilt
or leakage limit.

The weak-limit passage explicitly needs atomlessness at EVERY level of
each canonical marginal. Uniform convergence over the shift follows by
subsequence compactness plus a moving-cap sandwich, and is valid under
the stated compact support. Rescaling a canonical unit normal to its
barycentric functional is harmless because the shift is free. The proof
does not assume a rate for weak convergence, point movement, or normal
movement.

The canonical own-cap upper bound localizes every q-maximizer by O(t).
The lower asymptotic retains the nonnegative original normal excess,
forcing limiting minimizing normals into canonical directions without
discarding a term of unknown rate. The uniform own-cap derivative has
the correct sign and coefficient kappa=d V[d/(d+1)]^(d-1). Averaging
the fixed canonical upper inequalities cancels the displacement; the
separate inequalities and their zero-sum slacks force the unique
first-order displacement for every maximizing selection.

Checked the explicit parallelogram area t, all three atomless limiting
marginals, the costs (1,1/3,0), and the displacement (-1/6,-2/3).
The three canonical second-order coefficients 25/72,97/72,2/9 are
correct. The threshold t<1/128 is exactly sufficient for the second
coordinate cap to remain above the small fibers at the moved point.
These checks do not replace the all-normal argument.

The global maximum Gamma V+t max(a,c) is a separate finite-cover result
in this particular support. The heavier anchor is uniquely maximizing
when a!=c; the equal case correctly allows an additional maximizer at
q. The conditional point-mass examples therefore establish the stated
LOCAL weak-limit obstruction only. the contributor's independently proved seven-
base example upgrades that phenomenon to a global obstruction.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
